# Disagreement Log — 1 Clement Chapter 7

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 7:2 "empty and vain" vs. "empty and futile" vs. "empty, futile"

- **EMET:** "empty and vain thoughts"
- **LOGOS:** "empty and futile reasonings"
- **PNEUMA:** "empty, futile thinking"
- **Greek:** *kenous kai mataiaislogismous* — empty and futile/vain reasonings
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "empty and futile thoughts." "Futile" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is better than "vain" (EMET) for *mataios*; "thoughts" is better than "reasonings" for *logismoi* in context.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 7:2 "rule" vs. "rule" vs. "standard"

- **EMET:** "glorious and holy rule of our tradition"
- **LOGOS:** "glorious and holy rule of our tradition"
- **PNEUMA:** "glorious and holy standard of our heritage"
- **Greek:** *ton semnon kai hagion kanona tēs paradoseōs hēmōn* — the venerable and holy canon/rule of our tradition
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "glorious and holy rule of our tradition." "Rule" (EMET/LOGOS) preserves *kanōn* precisely. "Heritage" (PNEUMA) for *paradosis* loses the sense of received tradition.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 7:3 "made us" vs. "who made us" — relative clause

- Minor structural disagreement. All agents agree on content. Recorded.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 7:4 "look steadfastly" vs. "gaze intently" vs. "look steadily"

- **EMET:** "look steadfastly at the blood of Christ"
- **LOGOS:** "gaze intently at the blood of Christ"
- **PNEUMA:** "look steadily at the blood of Christ"
- **Greek:** *atenisōmen eis to haima tou Christou* — let us look intently at the blood
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "look steadfastly at the blood of Christ." *Atenizō* = to gaze fixedly; "steadfastly" captures sustained attention better than "steadily."

---

## Disagreement 5 — 7:4 "shed for our salvation" vs. "poured out" — verb

- **EMET:** "being shed for our salvation"
- **LOGOS:** "being poured out for our salvation"
- **PNEUMA:** "shed for our salvation"
- **Greek:** *ekchutheisa dia tēn sōtērian hēmōn* — having been poured out for our salvation
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "being shed for our salvation." Both "shed" and "poured out" are common renderings; "shed" is the traditional English phrase for blood.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 7:4 "won for the whole world" vs. "brought to the whole world" vs. "brought"

- **EMET:** "it won for the whole world the grace of repentance"
- **LOGOS:** "it brought to the whole world the grace of repentance"
- **PNEUMA:** "it brought the grace of repentance to the whole world"
- **Greek:** *pantos tou kosmou tēs metanoias charin ēnegken* — bore/brought the grace of repentance to all the world
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "it won for the whole world the grace of repentance." *Pherō* = to bear/carry/bring; "won" (EMET) is interpretive; "brought" (LOGOS) is more literal.
- **Revised ruling:** SOPHIA uses "it brought to the whole world the grace of repentance" (LOGOS). More literal.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 7:5 "Sovereign Lord" vs. "Master" vs. "the Lord"

- **EMET:** "the Master"
- **LOGOS:** "the Sovereign Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "the Lord"
- **Greek:** *ho despotēs* — the master/sovereign
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the Sovereign Lord." *Despotēs* is Clement's characteristic term for God, distinct from *kyrios*. "Sovereign Lord" captures both the authority (*despotēs*) and the divine dignity.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 7:5 "pass in review" vs. "review" vs. "go through"

- **EMET:** "review all the generations"
- **LOGOS:** "pass in review all the generations"
- **PNEUMA:** "go through every generation in history"
- **Greek:** *episkepsōmetha panta genea* — let us look over/review every generation
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "pass in review all the generations" (LOGOS). The formal phrase suits the deliberate survey that follows.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 7:6 "preached" vs. "proclaimed" vs. "preached"

- **EMET/PNEUMA:** "preached repentance"
- **LOGOS:** "proclaimed repentance"
- **Greek:** *metanoian ekēruzen* — preached/proclaimed repentance (*kēryssō*)
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "preached repentance." *Kēryssō* = to herald/preach; consistent with other uses in the letter.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 7:7 "foreign to God" vs. "strangers to God" vs. "outsiders with no prior claim on God"

- **EMET:** "foreign to God"
- **LOGOS:** "strangers to God"
- **PNEUMA:** "outsiders, with no prior claim on God"
- **Greek:** *allotrioi tou theou* — strangers/foreigners to God
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "strangers to God" (LOGOS). PNEUMA's gloss is interpretive. "Strangers" best captures the alien relationship of the Ninevites to Israel's God.

---

*End of disagreement log for 1 Clement Chapter 7.*
